svg.text: Three request shapes on one connection: request/response, streams, and unsolicited runtime events.
supervisor.rs finds or spawns the profile's server
connect — unix socket, or ssh <host> … relay stdio
strict equality — any other version is Refused, and only a newer client may evict
SetEnvOverlay { SSH_AUTH_SOCK, DISPLAY, TERM, LANG, LC_* }
a daemonised server has none of these of its own
153 of them — one task per request, replies may come back out of order
a stream is opened once, then driven by plain commands on its id
spawn PTY — login shell in the worktree
the response reaches the wire before the forwarder starts, so no frame can precede the id that names it
the stream is opened first, the turn is launched second
take the stashed launch params, launch
persisted to SQLite, then fanned out
recovery is server-side — the client is never told a lag happened
one subscription to the runtime, fanned out to every attached client
the sessions and terminals keep running on the far side
terminalAttach / attachSession on the ids it kept
fresh stream ids over the same live PTYs and sessions
dashed = a return or a pushed event
